sections.html: Trichomycterus alternatus reaches about 10 cm and resembles a loach with a walrus's moustache.

Size: 8.0 cm.

Temperature: 24–28°C.

pH: 6.0–7.0.

Family: Trichomycteridae.

IUCN Red List: Least Concern (LC). Trichomycterus alternatus is widely distributed, frequent and abundant in the Paraíba do Sul River basin and coastal rivers from the states of Rio de Janeiro to Paraná. However, the high degree of degradation of the basins imposes diffuse threats on the different subpopulations of the species, which cannot yet be quantified but must be monitored. As current knowledge of these threats does not indicate a risk of extinction, the species has been listed as Least Concern (IUCN 2022).
Trichomycterus alternatus comes from Brazil. The fish originate from fast-running brooks.

South America: Atlantic coastal river basins, Rio de Janeiro and Espírito Santo States, Jequitinhonha River basin, Minas Gerais, Brazil. Type locality: Rio Doce, near the village Rio Doce, Minas Gerais, Brazil [20°14'41"S, 42°53'45"W].
The water temperature can be between 22 and 25°C. No special requirements for the aquarium water are needed, but it should be clean and oxygen-rich.
As the fish originate from fast-running brooks, they like a good filter current.

Will feed on most aquarium fare such as tablet, frozen and live foods. It is an opportunistic predator that mainly feeds on insects, but also will take small crustaceans and plant material (algae and remains of phanerogams).
Regarding feeding, this loach-catfish is completely unproblematic.
The species likes the company of its own kind and should always be kept in groups. Otherwise the fish will be shy and hiding.

Males and females are coloured differently; moreover, males have longer and broader pectoral fins. Both the sexual dimorphism and the juvenile coloration are very similar to the stone loach (Barbatula barbatula).

The best-known of the feared species of fish in South America is the so-called candiru. In fact, the name candiru is applied to a number of different species in different genera, but this does not matter in this context. The candiru is able to penetrate the ureter of a human if the person is urinating under water. This causes horrible infections that can even be fatal. The fish has spines on the operculum which make it impossible to move backwards. So the candiru dies in the ureter and the victim is harmed from inside.

Of course this is not the real intention of the candiru. Its aim is to find one of the giant catfishes and suck blood from their gills. When a candiru swims into a human's ureter this is only an accident. Nevertheless, being a bloodsucking parasite does not make the candiru more likeable.

This is sad, because some of the close relatives of the candiru are charming and interesting aquarium inhabitants. One of them is Trichomycterus alternatus from Brazil.

Description: Body cross-section oval near head, gradually compressed posteriorly towards caudal fin. Body elongate with dorsal and ventral profiles slightly convex on trunk and nearly straight along caudal peduncle. Body depth approximately even along entire body, only slightly decreasing posterior to dorsal-fin origin (Vinícius et al. 2019).

Etymology: The specific name alternatus is Latin for alternated, referring to 10–14 large spots along the middle of the sides, frequently alternating with a series of spots above them and sometimes partly confluent with them, forming a longitudinal series or a series of irregular bars across the back.
